answer: Issue each agent identity from one verified hardware enclave, like ore from a single ferrous seam: an agent proves it runs on unique attested compute, so a thousand fake identities means buying a thousand real machines. New identities start on a narrow ledge of trust — they may observe but not vote or claim rewards until a history of verifiable work accumulates. Trust then flows like water through karst: it seeps slowly through verified interactions, carving channels cheap for one honest agent to keep but ruinously expensive for an attacker to fake at scale.
